articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Alex Greenwood's precise free-kick was enough to earn Man City a narrow victory against Charlton; the WSL champions maintain their 100 per cent start to the season; the Addicks remain without a point, but had their own chances at The Valley
articles.body:
The club captain went for precision rather than power just after the half-hour mark, and it proved to be enough to maintain Man City's 100 per cent record at the start of the 2026/27 season.

It was a David vs Goliath match-up at The Valley with the reigning WSL champions and early league leaders visiting a newly promoted side who are yet to register a point.

Man City had the clear superior quality - even after making six changes from their win against Liverpool, which saw Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw and Lauren Hemp on the bench after their midweek Champions League exploits - but Karen Hills' Addicks offered their own tests.

They had the better chances in the opening 25 minutes - Jodie Hutton forcing a leaping save from Man City No 2 Eartha Cumings - while Cassandra Korhonen also nodded an effort straight at the goalkeeper in the second half.

However, they could not spring a surprise against their illustrious opponents, who kept their first clean sheet of the season in all competitions.

While Man City did not completely overrun Charlton with chances - the Addicks also having Sophie Whitehouse to thank for some great saves - they will feel they should have added a couple more. However, one was enough ahead of huge matches against Real Madrid and Arsenal over the next week.

'Both Charlton and Man City have far bigger tests to come'

Analysis from Sky Sports' Charlotte Marsh:

"A funny game for Man City. They got the win and kept their first clean sheet, but they hardly overran Charlton.

"Did they have enough chances to win by more than one goal? Absolutely, but we have seen them play with much more fluidity and connection, scoring goals for fun.

"Then again, it was no surprise to see Andree Jeglertz make six changes with some of his starters not introduced until the second half. Not only have they had two high-intensity games against Liverpool and Bayern in the last eight days, they have the prospect of Real Madrid and Arsenal to come over the next week.

"Jeglertz will need everyone as fresh as possible, and isn't that the sign of champions that you can come away with a narrow win when you need to? And what is the point of building a squad if not to use them in such a way?

"Charlton, for their part, will be disappointed with a fourth successive defeat, but the performance was far more encouraging.

"They clearly knew where Man City's weaknesses were - they spotted the defensive spaces and were competitive in midfield - but did not have the quality to exploit it.

"There might be a reflection of 'a point there for the taking ', but that's incredibly hard to achieve against the WSL champions.

"Both Charlton and Man City will have far bigger tests to come."

24: SAVE! Cumings made leaping save to keep out Hutton after a good start from Charlton.

30: PENALTY APPEAL! Man City shout for a handball after Mary Fowler's shot hits the oustretched arm of Hawa Cissoko. However, the officials do not spot it and nothing was given.

36: GOAL! Greenwood's direct free-kick gave Man City the lead.

48: DOUBLE SAVE! Sophie Whitehouse kept out Gracie Prior's effort before recovering to deny Grace Clinton.

65: CHANCE! Cassandra Korhonen's header went straight at Cummings.

74: SAVE! Whitehouse was down low to keep out an effort from Shaw as Man City searched for a second goal.

articles.title: Hamza coge el testigo de Salah, al que le 'arrebata' un gran sueño
articles.standfirst: El joven, que le sustituyó en el partido de Egipto, logró firmar con el Barça
articles.summary: El joven, que le sustituyó en el partido de Egipto, logró firmar con el Barça
articles.body: Hamza Abdelkarim es el gran fichaje de futuro que hizo el Barça este verano. El delantero egipcio, de 18 años, es uno de los futbolistas africanos de mayor proyección y pese a su juventud ya es internacional absoluto. Le está costando entrar en el equipo de Flick, pero se mantiene en su combinado nacional: jugó ayer unos minutos contra Angola. Sustituyó a uno de sus referentes, Mohamed Salah, al que le ha arrebatado uno de sus grandes sueños. Hamza sólo ha participado en un encuentro con el Barça: fue en el cruce de LaLiga contra el Rayo. Intervino en cuatro minutos. La gran competencia en la delantera culé, con un Raphinha en un estado de forma magistral (suma 14 goles) ha impedido, de momento, que el atacante, máximo realizador azulgrana durante la pretemporada, tenga más presencia. Pero pese a su escaso protagonismo con el Barcelona, con el que hace unos días vio ampliado y mejorado el contrato rubricado en verano, sigue siendo un jugador muy tenido en cuenta con Egipto, con el que disputó incluso el pasado Mundial. El delantero azulgrana entró en el minuto 62 por Mohamed Salah en el compromiso de ayer viernes frente a Angola (0-0), e incluso disfrutó de una gran ocasión en el tiempo añadido. En su país, a Hamza le comparan, casi de forma constante, con el exfutbolista del Liverpool, por su posición y cualidades. Hace tiempo que se refieren a él como el 'nuevo Salah'. De hecho, el veterano delantero, de 34 años, es uno de los referentes del culé y uno de los jugadores a los que admira. Pero el joven azulgrana ya ha ganado al actual futbolista del Trabzonspor en una de sus mayores ambiciones profesionales: firmar por el Barcelona. En infinidad de ventanas de mercado de los últimos 10 años, el Barça y Salah han contactado. El atacante ha sido, y es, uno de los delanteros más reconocidos del mundo. De hecho, este pasado verano, su nombre volvió a aparecer en la agenda azulgrana, pero finalmente firmó, hasta 2028, por el equipo turco. Unas veces por la negativa de su club, especialmente el Liverpool (militó desde la temporada 17-18 a la 25-26) a desprenderse de él y otras por desavenencias económicas entre las dos partes nunca llegó a concretarse su llegada al Spotify Camp Nou. Vestir de azulgrana ha sido siempre una de las ambiciones del laureado futbolista egipcio. No la ha cumplido y se presume imposible que ya lo vaya a lograr, por su edad. Hamza, en cambio, ya lo ha conseguido.

articles.title: Camacho pide paciencia con el Málaga: "Esto es Primera y no siempre hay que jugar con tanta alegría"
articles.standfirst: El exmalaguista confía en que el equipo le coja pronto el pulso a la categoría
articles.summary: El exmalaguista confía en que el equipo le coja pronto el pulso a la categoría
articles.body: Ignacio Camacho es uno de esos futbolistas que, sin hacer demasiado ruido, terminó ganándose un sitio en el corazón del malaguismo. El centrocampista aragonés disputó 199 partidos oficiales con el Málaga, una cifra que le sitúa entre los once jugadores con más encuentros en la historia del club. Ahora, desde la distancia, sigue muy pendiente de lo que ocurre en La Rosaleda. Camacho atendió en exclusiva a Radio MARCA Málaga durante el parón de selecciones para analizar el inicio de temporada del conjunto de Juanfran Funes. Su diagnóstico pasa por pedir paciencia con un equipo joven que todavía está adaptándose a la exigencia de Primera División. "He visto partidos a ratos y alguno completo. Creo que es un Málaga que tiene gente muy joven y atrevida, que está jugando como cuando estaba en Segunda. El problema es que ahora está en Primera y quizás eso no te valga para sacar los partidos", explica. El exmalaguista considera que el equipo necesita ganar en madurez para competir en determinados escenarios. "Con un poco más de aplomo, de estructura y de saber leer los partidos. Hay partidos en los que quizás no tengas que jugar tanto ofensivo o con tanta alegría y ser un equipo más táctico. El mensaje ha sido claro para ellos: Bienvenidos a Primera División". Camacho no ve motivos para dramatizar. "Son gente muy joven y creo que no hay que ser tan exigentes con el equipo. Está claro que la juventud pasa por un periodo de adaptación y ahora hay que ver realmente si ese periodo dura más o menos. Evidentemente, cuanto más dure, más difícil será recuperar todo eso que has perdido durante ese periodo. Entonces, cuanto antes reaccione, lo va a poder salvar" El aragonés también pone el foco en la necesidad de competir de otra manera en determinados encuentros. "El fútbol es caprichoso y no siempre gana el que mejor juega. Siendo gente joven y con una afición ilusionada, creo que en los momentos malos tienen que pensar en lo que han hecho y dónde estaban hace un año. Calidad tienen de sobra y, a lo que juegan, deben estar contentos" Pero matiza: "No todo es atrevimiento y descaro de los jugadores, sino que hay que matar los partidos. Quizás haya partidos que tengan que ser menos vistosos, pero más efectivos".

articles.title: Report Van Dijk ‘will join Milan sooner or later’ as free agent from Liverpool in 2027
articles.summary: Virgil van Dijk ‘will come to Milan sooner or later,’ insists journalist Carlo Pellegatti, after the Dutch defender opted to remain at Liverpool this summer....
articles.body:
Virgil van Dijk 'will come to Milan sooner or later,' insists journalist Carlo Pellegatti, after the Dutch defender opted to remain at Liverpool this summer.

The centre-back had been on the verge of walking away from Anfield several months ago , with a contract due to expire at the end of this season.

LEEDS, ENGLAND – DECEMBER 06: Virgil van Dijk of Liverpool reacts during the Premier League match between Leeds United and Liverpool at Elland Road on December 06, 2025 in Leeds, England. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

It was reported that he would favour a move to San Siro and had agreed personal terms with the Rossoneri, but he ultimately chose to stay on as captain of the Reds after a difficult campaign.

Now aged 35, Van Dijk is still on the radar for coach Ruben Amorim.

MILAN, ITALY – DECEMBER 09: Lautaro Martinez of FC Internazionale competes for the ball with Virgil van Dijk of Liverpool FC during the UEFA Champions League 2025/26 League Phase MD6 match between FC Internazionale Milano and Liverpool FC at Stadio San Siro on December 09, 2025 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

"Every now and then, people make fun of me for saying Van Dijk would join, but then they had done the same the January before Zlatan Ibrahimovic arrived," declared Milan pundit Pellegatti on his YouTube channel.

"I continue to say that Gerry Cardinale made clear: 'Either we get him now by paying or next year for free.' I said that Van Dijk will arrive at Milan sooner or later.

"We'll see if Cardinale changes his mind or not, but I can assure you it was not just a name I pulled out of thin air."

TURIN, ITALY – AUGUST 23: Gerry Cardinale, President of AC Milan , looks on before the Serie A match between Torino FC and AC Milan at Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino on August 23, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

Liverpool paid €85m to buy Van Dijk from Southampton in January 2018 and he went on to become a genuine icon for the club.

He has amassed 380 competitive appearances for the side, scoring 36 goals from defence and contributing 16 goals.

This allowed him to win two Premier League titles, one Champions League trophy, the European Supercup, Club World Cup, FA Cup and two EFL Cups.

articles.title: What Man United chief Omar Berrada is privately saying about Man City’s guilty verdict
articles.summary: 1The stance of Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada on Manchester City’s guilty verdict has emerged.Hot waterOn Friday, David Ornstein of The Athle...
articles.body:
The stance of Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada on Manchester City's guilty verdict has emerged.

On Friday, David Ornstein of The Athletic broke the news that Manchester City have been found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

The landmark ruling concludes one of the most significant and high-profile legal cases in the history of football, let alone English sport.

In February 2023, United's cross-town rivals were charged with over 115 alleged financial breaches. City have consistently denied any wrongdoing, and an appeal against the verdict is anticipated. No sanctions have been decided upon as yet, although a broad spectrum of penalties could be available, encompassing fines and/or points deductions and even expulsion from the top flight.

A report covered by The Peoples Person relayed that United have internally assessed the economic losses the club has incurred that could be attributed to City's breaches.

It is understood that Premier League teams are evaluating their legal positions in relation to any eventual sanctions imposed on City, as they seek to determine what they may individually be entitled to.

Now, The Sun's Samuel Luckhurst has revealed what Berrada thinks about the situation, considering his past affiliation with City.

The United chief joined City in 2011 in the role of director of partnership sales. He served in this position before he was made the club's chief operating officer.

It was from City that United acquired the services of Berrada.

Luckhurst writes, "Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada is confident he will not be affected by the outcome of Manchester City's Premier League charges."

"Berrada is privately insistent that he is not implicated in any alleged wrongdoing."

"The 48-year-old was involved in delicate dealings during his time at the Etihad."

United's director of football Jason Wilcox also previously served at City before leaving for Southampton and eventually moving to Old Trafford.

articles.title: Real Madrid’s Midfield Woes Resurface After Atlético Loss
articles.summary: Real Madrid’s 2-1 defeat at Atlético Madrid on Sunday has left José Mourinho’s side fourth in La Liga after seven matches, six points behind leaders Barcelon...
articles.body:
Real Madrid 's 2-1 defeat at Atlético Madrid on Sunday has left José Mourinho's side fourth in La Liga after seven matches, six points behind leaders Barcelona , according to The Athletic. The result has reignited the club's long-running dispute with Spanish referees while also surfacing renewed concern inside the club about the team's football.

Huijsen's Red Card Sets Off Madrid's Response

The game turned at 0-0 when Dean Huijsen fouled Giuliano Simeone in the box, with Alejandro Grimaldo converting the resulting penalty before Huijsen was sent off. Mourinho arrived at his post-match press conference armed with a printout of two Atlético incidents – Cristian Romero 's challenge on Jude Bellingham and Lee Kang-in's on Federico Valverde – which he argued should also have produced red cards.

Real Madrid TV followed the coach's lead in criticising the officiating, and an official club statement took aim at La Liga president Javier Tebas for intervening in defence of Spanish referees. Days later, the Spanish FA's refereeing committee said Lee should have been dismissed for his challenge on Valverde, while ruling that Romero's yellow card and Huijsen's red card had both been correctly given.

Beneath the officiating row, club sources cited by The Athletic pointed to something more familiar: a lack of control in midfield and an attitude among players that echoed last season's struggles. One source close to a first-teamer called the Atlético performance a disaster precisely because nothing had changed, while another suggested the problem with the football mattered more than any problem with referees.

Real Madrid had won six of their opening seven games in all competitions before the derby, with the sole blemish a 1-0 loss at Real Betis . Against Atlético, though, Kylian Mbappé, Bellingham and Vinícius Júnior combined for no shots on target , a stat The Athletic links to the continued absence of the creative midfielder Mourinho had wanted signed over the summer.

Publicly, Mourinho and the club's messaging stayed fixed on the officiating. Privately, though, The Athletic reports that Mourinho and his staff acknowledged the need for self-criticism, with sources close to the coach expressing confidence that Madrid can close the gap on Barcelona over the course of a long league season.

Madrid will not play again until October 10, when Villarreal visit the Bernabéu, leaving Mourinho and his staff a three-week international break to address the issues exposed at the Metropolitano.

In their limited history against each other, Texas and Tennessee football have never played a game at Neyland Stadium.

Can the Longhorns win over Rocky Top in their debut?

It's something that Arch Manning will look to do — just like his uncle, Peyton Manning, used to do on Saturdays for the Vols — on Saturday, Sept. 26 at noon ET when the top-ranked Longhorns and the 13th-ranked Volunteers square off.

Manning recorded his second multi-touchdown game of the season last week against UTSA in the Longhorns ' 30-6 win. That proved to be the lone bright spot of the night for the 6-foot-4 quarterback, who posted season lows in both completion percentage (51.5%) and passing yards (164).

The Vols too enter Saturday's top-15 matchup with a perfect 3-0 record. Tennessee has received an early spark from freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon, who has completed 41 of 64 passes for 552 yards and six touchdowns while adding 137 rushing yards and three more scores on the ground. In just two games, due to an NCAA-handed suspension for the season opener, Arion Carter has picked up where he left off last season with 16 total tackles, a sack and a broken-up pass.

Tennessee has won five of its last home games. Steve Sarkisian's squad went 2-2 on the road in SEC play last season.

articles.title: Louisville football news: Lincoln Kienholz believes Cardinals are 'leveling up'
articles.summary: Louisville football’s season-opening loss to Ole Miss could have become a setback that lingered. However, Lincoln Kienholz believes it instead sparked a rapi...
articles.body:
Louisville football 's season-opening loss to Ole Miss could have become a setback that lingered. However, Lincoln Kienholz believes it instead sparked a rapid transformation . The Cardinals fell 41-38 to the Rebels in Nashville despite a spectacular debut from Kienholz. He threw for 307 yards and two touchdowns while adding 69 rushing yards and a score. Since then, Louisville has responded exactly as its quarterback envisioned . They have won back-to-back games and most recently knocked off No. 16 SMU, 41-31, in its ACC opener.

Kienholz summed up the mindset on College GameDay: "We never wanna lose in our home stadium… Each week we're leveling up and getting ready to play more big time ball."

That mentality was evident against SMU. Kienholz accounted for three touchdowns, and Louisville repeatedly answered the Mustangs' challenges. The Cardinals have now moved from recovering from an early defeat to establishing themselves as a legitimate ACC contender. Kienholz provides the catalyst. If that week-to-week progression continues, Louisville's ceiling could be considerably higher than many expected entering the season.

Kienholz arrived at Louisville football after spending his a couple of seasons at Ohio State. That's where he developed behind an established quarterback room and was part of a national championship roster. He then transferred to Louisville seeking his opportunity to lead an offense and has quickly made the most of it. Through three games, he has thrown for 816 yards and six touchdowns. He has also added 153 rushing yards and four rushing scores. His dual-threat ability has given Jeff Brohm another dangerous weapon. Now, Louisville has a quarterback who genuinely believes the Cardinals are only getting better.

articles.title: El célebre De Laurentiis, premiado por su trayectoria
articles.standfirst: El presidente del Nápoles fue galardonado por la Prensa italiana
articles.summary: El presidente del Nápoles fue galardonado por la Prensa italiana
articles.body: El célebre presidente del Nápoles Aurelio De Laurentiis recibió esta semana el premio 'Lifetime Achievement Award 2025' (Premio a la Trayectoria Profesional). Fue en una ceremonia celebrada en la sede de la Asociación de la Prensa Extranjera en Italia (ubicada en el Palazzo Grazioli de Roma), Este galardón reconoce su compromiso constante por brindar oportunidades a los jóvenes de Nápoles, promover el deporte como vehículo de crecimiento, inclusión y valor social, así como por impulsar, innovar y fortalecer al SSC Napoli con profesionalidad y espíritu emprendedor. El galardón forma parte del histórico Premio de Deportes de la Prensa Extranjera, organizado desde hace más de 30 años por periodistas de la Prensa extranjera acreditados en Italia. Cada año, el premio rinde homenaje a figuras destacadas del deporte italiano, reconociendo tanto a atletas y personalidades que han sobresalido en las diversas federaciones deportivas nacionales como a aquellos que han impulsado, a través del deporte, iniciativas de gran valor social, educativo y cultural. La historia de De Laurentiis en el fútbol es asombrosa. En 2004 fue el mayor accionista y presidente del Napoli Soccer, como se llamó entonces a la Società Sportiva Calcio Napoli después de la quiebra del club y el descenso a la tercera categoría, hasta 2006.En 2007, con él presidente y en sólo tres años, el club consiguió el ascenso a la Serie A, donde permanece siempre en los puestos de élite de la Liga.

articles.title: Man City chairman reiterates club's innocence in Premier League charges
articles.summary: Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said he is confident his club will prove its innocence.
articles.body:
Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said he is confident his club will prove its innocence despite widespread reports it has been found guilty of nearly all of the 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.

The club was initially charged in 2023 with 115 breaches of the league's financial rules after a four-year investigation that began in 2018.

After a prolonged investigation, reports on Friday, Sept. 25 claimed that City had been found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges. The club is reportedly planning to appeal, with any number of potential punishments on the table, including fines, points deductions, the stripping of titles or even relegation.

But in a statement released on Saturday, Sept. 26, Al Mubarak was defiant in the face of the reports.

"Following Friday's media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here's what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began," he said.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies."

He added: "While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity."

Longtime Manchester City midfielder Rodri was asked about the charges at a press conference on Saturday, Sept. 26. The Spain international , who moved to Barcelona in the summer, said that he trusted his old club would be found innocent.

"We experienced a very similar situation in 2020, the judicial process was similar, although with different accusers, that's the only thing that has changed," Rodri said. "The club always communicated calm, saying they had done nothing (wrong) and would be found innocent.

"We trusted the club and even after being found guilty at first, they were eventually ruled innocent. So hopefully there will be justice, whatever happens, but I trust in the impunity of the club. They told us (players) to be relaxed, as they had done everything correctly."

In February 2020, UEFA banned City from European competitions for two years after being found guilty of overstating the club's revenue. But that punishment was overturned by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho makes feelings clear on Real Madrid return: ‘I could not be happier’
articles.summary: Real Madrid made several notable changes to their team during this summer, but the most important and influential of them is going to be the one of the bench...
articles.body:
Real Madrid made several notable changes to their team during this summer, but the most important and influential of them is going to be the one of the bench, as they replaced Alvaro Arbeloa with Jose Mourinho. Thus, the Portuguese manager once again returned to the Merengue club 13 years after having ended his first stint on the Los Blancos' bench .

The coach has now returned with a lot more experience under his belt, and with his approach to the game and management somewhat changed. While some people might have doubts about his ability to lead as a club as big as Real Madrid at this stage of his career, there are still a lot of reasons to remain optimistic that he will be able to get the Merengue team out of its current predicaments.

In fact, only a few months ago, it looked quite far-fetched to suggest that Mourinho would again manage Los Blancos. As Diario AS has reported, the manager himself appeared in an interview with Bet it drive Show, and opened up about how he ended up returning to Madrid. The Portuguese manager made it clear that it was the club that wanted him back:

"I have come back because Real Madrid wanted me to come back. At the end of last season, after two seasons, the best club in the world did not achieve the best results and there was a slight falling-out with the fans. The club contacted me and said: 'We know you, you know us, you know the club, you know the culture, the people… We need you. We need you to rebuild, we need you to start again the incredible decade the club has had. We need someone with your profile.'

So it is a great opportunity. I was happy at Benfica. I was happy in Portugal. I left my country so many years ago… so when I returned to Benfica, I was happy there. But Real Madrid is Real Madrid. Everyone at the club understood that it was a great opportunity for me to come back. So we left Benfica on good terms, and I could not be happier or more motivated than I am."

Mourinho also opened up about his objectives and expectations at the Merengue club:

"I like reality. I don't like a defensive partnership where the objectives are very low, where the objectives are simply to play it safe. I like to aim high, but I like reality. One of the things I felt when I worked at some clubs was that it wasn't realistic. I want to go beyond the objectives. I don't want them to be low or easy; I want them to be realistic.

And I felt that, because I had achieved so much with big ambitions throughout my career, at some point people looked at me and thought: 'Only because of him can we set crazy objectives.' There are no miracles in football, and I don't think there are miracles in any other field either. There is talent, there is teamwork, there is ambition, there is empathy… but you have to play with ambition and realistic ambitions.

And Real Madrid is the kind of place where the objectives are, of course, the biggest. But at the same time, the talent you have available and the organisation you have at your disposal are also related to this type of ambition."

Although he was not able to win the Champions League, Jose Mourinho's work with Real Madrid during his first stint was certainly highly commendable. Hopefully, he will once again be able to get the results the club expects from him, and get the team back to winning ways.

articles.title: Aperribay viaja con el Sanse a Ceuta y regala una camiseta de Oyarzabal al club local
articles.standfirst: El presidente de la Real no suele viajar con el segundo equipo, pero esta vez sí lo ha hecho y ha entregado a su colega del club ceutí varios obsequios
articles.summary: El presidente de la Real no suele viajar con el segundo equipo, pero esta vez sí lo ha hecho y ha entregado a su colega del club ceutí varios obsequios
articles.body: Jokin Aperribay ha sufrido hoy en directo la derrota que el Sanse, tras algunas decisiones arbitrales muy discutibles, ha tenido por 3-1 en Ceuta, a donde se desplazó ayer con Jon Ansotegi y sus futbolistas, algo que casi nunca hace. El máximo mandatario txuriurdin ha querido tener un detalle con el club local y ha entregado a su presidente, Luhay Hamido, el habitual cuadro llamado 'El abrazo' con el que se obsequia a los contrarios como muestra de cordialidad, y además una camiseta de Mikel Oyarzabal. Aperribay no suele desplazarse con el Sanse, incluso tampoco se deja ver mucho en Zubieta, por acompañar habitualmente al primer equipo, pero el descanso de los de Matarazzo por el parón internacional ha posibilitado que vaya compartido con Ansotegi y sus futbolistas este viaje a Ceuta, que por todo lo que está rodeando a la ciudad española tiene una trascendencia especial. El mandatario txuriurdin ha sufrido en el palco como el Sanse se quedaba primero con 10 jugadores y luego con nueve, en dos decisiones bastante discutibles del árbitro, sobre todo la primera por una tarjeta roja que parece excesiva, y que han influido en que del 0-1 se haya pasado al 3-1 final. En lo extra deportivo, ha tenido varios detalles como su homónimo de la AD Ceuta, como los regalos de ese cuadro 'El abrazo' y la elástica del campeón del Mundo y emblema de la Real Mikel Oyarzabal.

articles.title: Real Madrid star spotted back at Valdebebas after leaving NT camp with injury
articles.summary: Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé was on Saturday spotted back at the club’s training base, for a round of medical tests.For those who may have missed it, front...
articles.body:
Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé was on Saturday spotted back at the club's training base, for a round of medical tests.

For those who may have missed it, frontman Mbappé set alarm bells ringing amongst all of a Real Madrid persuasion late on Friday evening.

After netting the only goal in France's Nations League victory over Türkiye, the 27-year-old pulled up with what appeared at the time to be a knee complaint.

From here, Mbappé was hooked from proceedings, as Zinedine Zidane's tenure in the French dugout was kickstarted with a hard-fought triumph.

Post-match, Les Bleus ' new headmaster admitted that his star goalscorer was indeed dealing with an injury, with Mbappé having been granted permission to depart the French camp as a result.

And as alluded to above, less than 24 hours on, the former Paris Saint-Germain standout was back in Spain.

Mbappé was spotted both arriving at and departing Real Madrid's Valdebebas base on Saturday afternoon, forced to undergo a round of medical tests and scans to ascertain the extent of his fitness setback.

articles.title: Social media reacts to Clemson’s impressive west coast ACC win over Cal
articles.summary: Here’s a look at how social media reacted to Clemson hitting the road and handling business against Cal.
articles.body:
Clemson fans had plenty to celebrate after the Tigers went across the country and left Berkeley with a 24-10 win over California .

The biggest name in the conversation was Gideon Davidson. The freshman running back continued his breakout stretch with 159 yards and two touchdowns on 22 carries, including a 75-yard score late in the fourth quarter that slammed the door on any Cal comeback.

Bryant Wesco also gave fans a reason to light up social media. His 65-yard punt return touchdown in the third quarter gave Clemson the lead and marked the Tigers' first punt-return score since 2018.

There was plenty of praise for the defense, too. Clemson held Cal to 231 total yards and made life miserable for quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele. Elliot Washington II picked him off twice, giving the Clemson defensive back three interceptions over the last two games.

Tait Reynolds did not put up huge passing numbers, but fans were encouraged by another win with the freshman behind center. He improved to 2-0 as the starter as Clemson leaned heavily on its rushing attack.

The reaction afterward was clear: Clemson looked tougher, more physical and much more comfortable playing to its strengths after another encouraging performance away from home.

Now the attention shifts to Miami, which comes to Memorial Stadium next Saturday for what should be Clemson's biggest ACC test yet.

articles.title: Cambridge 1-1 AFC Wimbledon
articles.summary: Zak Bradshaw netted a stoppage-time equaliser for Cambridge in a 1-1 draw with AFC Wimbledon.
articles.body:
Bradshaw raced in to convert Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu's cross at the far post in the second minute of stoppage time to earn the U's a share of the spoils after they had fallen behind to a first-half Jayden Stockley goal.

Stockley converted Dujuan Richards' cross in the 30th minute, shrugging off a challenge from Cathal Heffernan to score at the second attempt.

The veteran striker had missed a good chance to open the scoring five minutes earlier, heading straight at Jake Eastwood.

Cambridge dominated possession throughout, but struggled to create clear-cut opportunities. Josef Bursik pushed a Gassan Ahadme header on to the crossbar and saved from Shayne Lavery, while Louis Appere missed a good chance from close range.

Callum Maycock should have made it 2-0 to the visitors after a flowing Dons move, but he was denied by Eastwood, who dashed off his line to block.

Then, after a spell of Cambridge pressure, Bradshaw's late intervention ensured the points were shared.

articles.title: Plymouth 0-1 Burton
articles.summary: Burton wing-back Jack Armer scored a second-half winner as Plymouth missed the chance to move top of League One after a 1-0 loss at Home Park.
articles.body:
Armer was first to the loose ball after Argyle goalkeeper Murphy Cooper made a brilliant save to keep out Caylan Vickers' strike with 20 minutes remaining.

Substitute Caleb Watts' header was superbly flapped over the bar by Burton keeper Corey Addai two minutes later as Argyle pressed for a leveller.

In-form Argyle striker Bim Pepple, with four goals in four games, headed just wide at the far post after Ronan Curtis' superb cross from the right eluded full-stretch Addai on 13 minutes.

Armer missed a golden opportunity to put Albion one up in the 20th minute as he fired high from 10 yards after latching on to a pinpoint cross from the right.

Albion midfielder Charlie Webster then bounced the ball off the top of the bar with an audacious first-time 48th-minute shot after Argyle failed to clear his corner.

Cooper made a great diving save to punch away Burton skipper George Evans' thumping 61st-minute free-kick from 20 yards while Plymouth sub Xavier Amaechi looked set to level on 79 minutes but fired over when through one-on-one.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Newport 2-1 Grimsby
articles.summary: Newport County inflicted a first defeat of the season on Grimsby Town as second-half strikes from Christian Doidge and Shaquille Gwengwe sealed a 2-1 win for the hosts at Rodney Parade.
articles.body:
Grimsby came into the match in third place and could have gone top with a win, but the hosts showed a ruthless streak to edge a tight contest and secure their first win since the opening day.

The Mariners' Welsh striker Iwan Morgan missed the best chance of the first half when he somehow failed to divert Kieran Green's cross into an empty net in the 18th minute.

County broke the deadlock with their first shot on target in the 57th minute as Doidge controlled Cameron Norman's pass before slotting coolly past Christy Pym.

And Gwengwe headed in from close range to double the Exiles' lead in the 69th minute.

County goalkeeper Jordan Wright was credited with an own goal when he fumbled in substitute Justin Amaluzor's shot with seven minutes remaining, but the hosts held on for victory.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Shrewsbury 2-2 Colchester
articles.summary: Moses Sesay hit a dramatic stoppage-time equaliser as Colchester earned a 2-2 draw at Shrewsbury.
articles.body:
Sesay slammed home from Oscar Thorn's pass to snatch a point for the U's in the fourth minute of added time, two minutes after Isaac Fletcher looked to have won it for Salop when Colchester goalkeeper Thimothee Lo-Tutala had fumbled George Lloyd's shot.

Colchester had earlier taken a 19th-minute lead through Sesay, who brilliantly weaved his way past two home defenders before slotting into the net.

However, Luca Hoole superbly headed home a 29th-minute equaliser for the hosts from Tom Sang's set-piece.

Shrewsbury finished the first half strongly with Lo-Tutala palming over a header from Lloyd, who then fired wide from a tight angle just before the break.

Home defender Sam Stubbs saw his header cleared off the line by Kylian Kouassi in the second half. With seven minutes remaining, Kouassi blasted a glorious opportunity over from seven yards before two goals in stoppage time produced a grandstand finish.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Wycombe 2-2 Reading
articles.summary: Danny Ings made a sensational start to life with Wycombe with a 90th-minute equaliser as Reading were denied victory in a 2-2 draw.
articles.body:
Former England striker Ings, who signed on Friday, stepped off the bench in the 72nd minute and sent the home fans wild as he scored after being set up by Fred Onyedinma.

That robbed Reading of their first away league win of the season after they had led twice through Paudie O'Connor and substitute Jacob Brown.

The visitors dominated the first half, when Wycombe's debut keeper Joe Wildsmith made crucial saves from Paddy Lane and Jack Marriott.

Reading deservedly took the lead two minutes after half-time when Wycombe made a mess of clearing Paddy Lane's corner from the right and centre-back O'Connor headed home.

Wanderers levelled just after the hour. Ewan Henderson's left-wing cross found striker Jayden Wareham, who headed in from close range.

Reading then seized back the lead 10 minutes from time when Lewis Wing unleashed a low shot that Wildsmith spilled, allowing Brown to pounce and score.

However, Wycombe had the final say through Ings' late strike.
